outcome: composite neonatal outcome (perinatal mortality, confirmed sepsis, grade III or IV intraventricular hemorrhage, retinopathy of prematurity, respiratory distress syndrome, bronchopulmonary dysplasia)
cohort: The study included 699 singleton pregnancies without major anomaly or aneuploidy, who had a cerclage placed at 10 institutions in the United States and Colombia between June 2016 and June 2020.
finding: The use of progestogen with cerclage was associated with significantly reduced rates of spontaneous preterm birth at <37 weeks and <34 weeks, increased latency to spontaneous delivery, and a lower frequency of perinatal death compared to cerclage alone.
gest_age: Spontaneous preterm birth at <37 weeks and <34 weeks were key outcomes, and gestational age at delivery was a secondary outcome.
